summary: Describes a high-level meeting location policy for the IETF and the stakeholders needed to carry it out.

plainLanguage.summary: This policy aims to spread IETF meetings across North America, Europe, and Asia over time. It also allows exploratory meetings, such as a meeting in another region or a virtual meeting, when the community supports the idea.

questions: what is an ietf exploratory meeting
what is the ietf 1-1-1 meeting policy
subtitle: Sets high-level guidance for rotating IETF meetings among regions, with room to explore.

tldr.problem: IETF meeting locations affect travel for in-person participants and time-zone difficulty for remote participants, but the regional rotation had not been formally defined.
tldr.mechanism: The policy aims to distribute meetings roughly equally among North America, Europe, and Asia over multiple years, while allowing exploratory meetings elsewhere or online.
tldr.outcome: The memo sets a consensus-backed high-level policy and outlines how exploratory proposals and venue selection proceed. Unit metadata lists RFC 9712 as an update.

today: RFC 8719 is a Best Current Practice and is updated by RFC 9712, according to the unit metadata.

sections.title: Why Meeting Locations Matter
sections.content:
IETF work mainly takes place on working-group mailing lists. In-person meetings provide a faster way to work through issues that remain unresolved.

Where meetings take place affects travel for people who attend in person and time-zone difficulty for people who participate remotely. This memo records a policy intended to distribute those effects among the regions where many participants have come from.
sections.plainLanguage: Most IETF work happens online, but in-person meetings help resolve difficult issues. The location affects both travel and the time zones faced by remote participants.

sections.title: The 1-1-1-* Meeting Policy
sections.content:
The regular policy aims to rotate meetings among North America, Europe, and Asia. It does not require a fixed regional order in each calendar year; instead, the distribution should be roughly equal over multiple years, with later choices seeking to rebalance earlier differences when possible.

The asterisk allows exploratory meetings. These can test another geographic region, a virtual meeting, or an additional meeting beyond the regular schedule.
sections.plainLanguage: The policy looks for a fair balance across three regions over several years, not a fixed schedule every year. It also leaves room to test other locations and virtual meetings.

sections.title: Proposing and Choosing a Venue
sections.content:
A person interested in an exploratory venue raises the proposal for community discussion. If the IETF chair finds consensus to pursue it, the proposal moves to the venue-selection discussion so interested people can refine it with logistical feedback.

The IESG decides whether an exploratory proposal can be implemented, in consultation with the IETF Administrative Support Activity. The venue-selection process chooses the actual location, and the decision is shared with the community for comment.
sections.plainLanguage: A new meeting idea first needs community support. The responsible groups then assess whether it can work, choose a venue, and report the decision back to the community.

sections.title: Reviewing the Policy
sections.content:
The memo expects participant distribution to change over time, so the policy should be reviewed periodically. Before revising it, the community should agree on the criteria to use.

The IASA is responsible for helping develop feasible meeting criteria and providing timely transparency about planned meetings so the community can give feedback.
sections.plainLanguage: The meeting policy may need revision as participation changes. The community should agree on review criteria first and receive timely information about planned meetings.
